claims.text: In nanoscale as-deposited non-equiatomic FeMnNiGeSi films and nanoribbons, magnetocaloric response and hysteresis are governed by nanoscale-modified magnetic domain structures.
Grain boundaries and surfaces enhance domain-wall pinning in the nanoscale FeMnNiGeSi material.
Enhanced domain-wall pinning alters exchange interactions and magnetic reversibility.
At high cycle frequencies, limited heat-transfer rates couple to the intrinsic microstructural effect and modify the response relative to bulk samples.
The as-deposited material has a disordered microstructure containing nanoscale grain boundaries.
Controlled annealing can modestly coarsen the grains and reduce surface-defect density without fully crystallizing the material.
Domain-wall pinning and exchange-interaction variations are mediated by nanoscale grain boundaries and surface defects.
Enhanced domain-wall pinning slows magnetic-reversal dynamics.
Slower magnetic reversal caused by pinning increases hysteresis during magnetocaloric cycles.
Reducing pinning sites by annealing shifts the magnetocaloric peak temperature.
Reducing pinning sites by annealing changes, and is expected to reduce, hysteresis width relative to the as-deposited baseline.
Heat-transfer limitations at higher cycle frequencies further modulate the effective magnetocaloric behavior.
The annealing-induced effect will be less pronounced at frequencies where heat-transfer limitations dominate.
The proposed mechanism applies in nanoscale geometries under applied fields of approximately 100 Oe or less.
Bulk samples or samples under high fields may follow a different mechanism because of different domain dynamics and thermal-transport properties.
There is no prior evidence for this alloy in a low-dimensional state under the specified magnetic-cooling conditions.
